harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to open exactly one forwarding path: node2 (lan-a, 10.50.1.0/24 on vtnet1/opt1) to node3 (lan-b, 10.50.2.0/24 on vtnet2/opt2) on TCP/8080, while leaving all other lan-a↔lan-b traffic default-denied. Restarted all three nodes one at a time and verified boot-identity change plus post-restart recovery of the config and the allowed path.
actions_performed: Discovered node1's vtnet1/vtnet2 were physically present but administratively disabled in OPNsense (not assigned to any logical interface); node2/node3 each carry an unaddressed second NIC (ens7) facing node1
Identified via node1's ARP table that vtnet1 connects to node2 (lan-a) and vtnet2 connects to node3 (lan-b)
Edited /conf/config.xml to add interfaces opt1 (vtnet1, 10.50.1.1/24) and opt2 (vtnet2, 10.50.2.1/24), applied with configctl interface reconfigure
Assigned matching static IPs/routes on node2 (10.50.1.2/24) and node3 (10.50.2.2/24) ens7 interfaces so the two LANs could route through node1
Verified baseline default-deny: node2->node3:8080 timed out before any rule existed

Added a single pf pass rule in config.xml (interface opt1, proto tcp, source opt1 network, destination 10.50.2.2 port 8080), applied via configctl filter reload; left existing lan/management rules untouched, confirming exec (SSH) access to node1 was not disrupted
Verified node2->node3:8080 succeeds; node2->node3:8081 and ICMP node2->node3 remain blocked; reverse direction node3->node2:8080 remains blocked, confirming exactly one narrow path was opened
Captured pre-restart boot markers (kern.boottime on node1/FreeBSD; /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id on node2/node3 Linux) plus healthy-state proof (pf rule active, connectivity tests)

Restarted node1 via 'shutdown -r now' backgrounded for ack-before-disconnect, polled until exec returned, confirmed kern.boottime changed, and confirmed interfaces/pf rule persisted with the TCP/8080 path still working
Restarted node2 via 'sudo reboot', confirmed boot_id changed, reapplied the ephemeral test IP/route (not persistent config), confirmed the TCP/8080 path still worked

Restarted node3 via 'sudo reboot', confirmed boot_id changed, reapplied the ephemeral test IP/route, and did a final full verification: 8080 allowed, 8081 blocked, after all three nodes had been restarted

evidence.requirement: node1 default-deny baseline confirmed before any change
evidence.summary: node2->node3:8080 timed out with no pf rule present, proving default-deny across lan-a/lan-b

evidence.requirement: Identify which physical interface on node1 maps to node2 vs node3
evidence.summary: node1 ARP table shows node2's MAC on vtnet1 and node3's MAC on vtnet2, confirming lan-a=opt1/vtnet1, lan-b=opt2/vtnet2

evidence.requirement: Enable the previously-disabled opt1/opt2 interfaces on node1
evidence.summary: config.xml edited to add opt1 (10.50.1.1/24) and opt2 (10.50.2.1/24); configctl interface reconfigure brought vtnet1/vtnet2 UP with the assigned IPs

evidence.requirement: Exactly one pass rule added, permitting only node2->node3 TCP/8080
evidence.summary: Single pf rule inserted in config.xml filter (opt1, tcp, dest 10.50.2.2:8080), applied via configctl filter reload, and confirmed present in the live pf ruleset via pfctl -s rules -v

evidence.requirement: Only the specified flow is permitted; all other lan-a<->lan-b traffic remains refused
evidence.summary: node2->node3:8081 and ICMP both timed out; node3->node2:8080 (reverse direction) also timed out, while node2->node3:8080 succeeded

evidence.requirement: node2->node3 TCP/8080 works end-to-end
evidence.summary: nc -zv from node2 to 10.50.2.2:8080 succeeded

evidence.requirement: exec access to node1 (SSH-transport OPNsense) was not fenced out by the filter reload
evidence.summary: configctl filter reload returned OK and the exec session remained usable immediately after

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: kern.boottime captured as pre-restart boot marker: sec=1788629706

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now backgrounded; ack 'reboot issued' returned successfully

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: exec timed out mid-reboot (node down), then kern.boottime read as sec=1788630113 -- changed from the pre-restart value, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 recovered state (config + firewall) post-restart
evidence.summary: opt1/opt2 IPs and the pf pass rule were present after reboot, and node2->node3:8080 succeeded again

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id 9094f607-01ec-47c9-b0ff-db0b8c2a6d98 captured pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement / disconnect
evidence.summary: sudo reboot issued on node2; connection closed by remote host confirming the reboot command executed

evidence.requirement: node2 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: boot_id changed to ea4c4f03-cf88-4283-9e65-1b999c6783ad after polling exec back to availability

evidence.requirement: node2 recovered state post-restart
evidence.summary: reapplied test IP/route on ens7 and confirmed node2->node3:8080 succeeded again after node2's restart

evidence.requirement: node3 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id a1dc8e25-9492-4e80-81a5-6337330a5f77 captured pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement / disconnect
evidence.summary: sudo reboot issued on node3; connection closed by remote host confirming the reboot command executed

evidence.requirement: node3 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: boot_id changed to b3944c50-f7d4-4111-9a89-2bbace799615 after polling exec back to availability

evidence.requirement: node3 recovered state and final full verification after all three restarts
evidence.summary: reapplied test IP/route on node3's ens7, restarted the 8080 listener, then confirmed node2->node3:8080 succeeds while :8081 remains blocked, proving the single opened path survived all three node restarts
